I merged it in, we're good for now. Now let's focus on this pilot I started but had to stop because we uncovered major bugs that are now fixed. I think this pilot is worth running so we can over threadloop's validity. Please rebase main then take a look at what we should do about this. # Plan ThreadLoop pilot build

> # ThreadLoop Consumer-Repository Feature Pilot Build Plan
>
> ## Summary
>
> The next ThreadLoop acceptance target is a supervised, real consumer-repository feature run:
>
> > Can Codex use the ThreadLoop runner skill while implementing a fresh feature in SignalPay, continue across separate wakes, preserve lifecycle and proof state, respond to current review evidence, and stop at `ready_for_human`?
>
> The pilot needs the runner skill and the existing ThreadLoop CLI. It does **not** need `runner-replay.test.ts`, a controller extracted from that test, or a new scheduler product.
>
> The role of each existing artifact is:
>
> - `.agents/skills/threadloop-runner/SKILL.md`: the procedure Codex follows for one explicit wake.
> - ThreadLoop CLI: lifecycle, proof, review, audit, and guarded-transition authority.
> - `tests/integration/runner-replay.test.ts`: ThreadLoop-internal regression coverage only; it is not installed, copied, imported, or executed by SignalPay.
> - The operator or a simple scheduled task: supplies the four wake inputs, retains the wake handoff, and starts the next Codex wake.
> - The human: retains approval, merge, recovery, and policy authority.
>
> This is intentionally a supervised pilot. A manually retained wake record and explicit invocations are sufficient to test whether the skill is usable. If the pilot later demonstrates that manual wake delivery is the dominant friction, that evidence can justify a separate controller or scheduler build.
>
> Current state on 2026-07-30:
>
> - ThreadLoop `origin/main` is `1312105dc860fe67c32eb207763fd262ff28282a`.
> - The runner skill is on `feat/issue-43-runner-contract@dce6d423bd790258ec09f84e3115b38632da8d6d`.
> - ThreadLoop PR #68 and issue #43 are closed, but the live consumer-repository pilot was not run.
> - SignalPay `main` is `a6e832cd8a5e031a3ea65729e04f1406ccf59b88`.
> - SignalPay PR #4 remains an open refund PR and is not the pilot target.
> - The current SignalPay checkout contains unrelated untracked local artifacts, so the pilot must use a fresh worktree.
>
> The intended review unit is the SignalPay pilot feature pull request. The runner skill must first be available from a reviewed, immutable ThreadLoop commit, but the pilot does not add ThreadLoop runtime code.
>
> ## Skills To Use
>
> - `software-build-plan`: keep the consumer pilot implementation-ready and separate from future automation.
> - `threadloop-runner`: govern each explicit Codex wake and enforce the one-action and human-authority boundaries.
> - `tdd-bdd`: require failing SignalPay behavior tests before production code.
> - `failure-path-testing`: prove idempotency, state-transition rejection, and no-mutation failure paths.
> - `workflow-invariants`: verify the wake, lifecycle, evidence, and authority boundaries throughout the run.
> - `dx-audit`: record setup burden, manual handoffs, unclear stops, and context-restart usability.
> - `code-review`: perform the mandatory final Standards and Spec review against the SignalPay feature fixed point.
>
> ## Scope
>
> ### In scope
>
> - Make the reviewed runner skill available in the fresh SignalPay worktree.
> - Use an immutable ThreadLoop package and signer commit SHA.
> - Create a dedicated SignalPay worktree and feature branch from current `origin/main`.
> - Start one explicit ThreadLoop session for one bounded feature.
> - Retain the four runner inputs and each wake result in a pilot handoff record.
> - Invoke Codex separately for each wake using the runner skill.
> - Have Codex write tests, implement one bounded feature, run focused checks, and create one scoped implementation commit when ThreadLoop authorizes `COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION`.
> - Run SignalPay’s immutable `make verify` gate through ThreadLoop.
> - Collect and import current signed CI and review evidence outside the runner wake.
> - Enter a bounded `COMMIT_REPAIR` wake only if the current review contains a legitimate blocking finding.
> - Start at least one later wake in a fresh Codex context to test continuity without transcript memory.
> - Stop at `ready_for_human` and export the verified audit trail.
> - Record technical success and developer-experience friction.
>
> The default fresh feature is **capture-state safety and retry semantics**:
>
> - Only an `authorized` payment can begin a new capture.
> - An exact idempotent retry of a successful capture returns the original response and emits no duplicate event.
> - A new idempotency key against a `captured` or `pending` payment fails without mutation or a new event.
> - Existing auth, scope, camelCase response, and event contracts remain stable.
>
> ### Out of scope
>
> - Extracting any code from `runner-replay.test.ts`.
> - Copying `runner-replay.test.ts` or a replay fixture into SignalPay.
> - Making the historical SignalPay PR #4 replay the pilot result.
> - Building a controller, scheduler, queue, lease service, agent launcher, provider abstraction, dashboard, or hosted service.
> - Changing ThreadLoop lifecycle, schema, protocol, CLI, or runtime packages.
> - Using the runner to push, open or merge a PR, approve, deploy, publish, rotate secrets, activate policy, or recover a blocked session.
> - Manufacturing a review defect solely to force a repair cycle.
> - Modifying, merging, or closing SignalPay PR #4.
> - Same-checkout multi-agent execution.
>
> ## Package Layout / File-to-Task Mapping
>
> ### ThreadLoop source
>
> - `.agents/skills/threadloop-runner/SKILL.md`: existing runner procedure copied or installed into SignalPay from the reviewed immutable ThreadLoop SHA.
> - `tests/integration/runner-replay.test.ts`: existing ThreadLoop-only regression. It remains where it is and is not a pilot dependency.
> - `.github/workflows/threadloop-gate-sensor.yml`: existing reusable signed gate sensor, pinned by full ThreadLoop commit SHA.
> - `.github/workflows/threadloop-review-sensor.yml`: existing reusable signed review sensor, pinned by the same full ThreadLoop commit SHA.
>
> No ThreadLoop source file is added or extracted for this pilot.
>
> ### SignalPay pilot
>
> - `.agents/skills/threadloop-runner/SKILL.md` **(new in the pilot worktree):** exact reviewed skill snapshot. Record its ThreadLoop source SHA in the file handoff or PR description.
> - `.github/workflows/threadloop.yml` **(new):** minimal caller workflow for the pinned ThreadLoop gate and review sensors.
> - `.threadloop/config.json` **(new):** visible repo-local ThreadLoop configuration. Commit it before the first runner wake.
> - `.plan/threadloop-capture-state-pilot/plan.md` **(new):** feature behavior, selected `PAY-*` rules, proof plan, and authority boundary.
> - `.plan/threadloop-capture-state-pilot/build-session-execution-plan.md` **(new):** ordered TDD and wake sequence.
> - `tests/test_payments_api.py` **(current):** capture-state and retry behavior tests.
> - `src/signalpay_api/app.py` **(current):** smallest production change that satisfies those tests.
>
> ### Pilot evidence outside the worktree
>
> - `wake-handoffs.jsonl` **(new, local-only):** one operator-retained record per wake containing the exact inputs, preflight facts, selected action, outcome, stop reason, and next authority.
> - Signed gate/review packages **(local-only):** downloaded and imported receipts, never treated as source code.
> - `threadloop-audit.jsonl` **(local-only unless deliberately attached to the pilot report):** verified ThreadLoop audit export.
> - `pilot-report.md` **(new, local-only during the run):** setup time, wake count, manual interventions, context-restart result, evidence friction, and final outcome.
>
> The handoff record is an operating artifact, not a new controller or product schema. The operator can append it manually after each wake.
>
> ## Dependencies And Settings
>
> - No new ThreadLoop runtime or development dependency.
> - No SignalPay package dependency, database, or Node project metadata.
> - Build the ThreadLoop CLI tarball from the reviewed full SHA and install it in a tool directory outside SignalPay, or invoke an already verified binary from that SHA.
> - Pin both reusable sensor workflows to the same reviewed full ThreadLoop SHA.
> - SignalPay remains Python 3.11+ with `uv`.
> - SignalPay’s immutable local gate is `make verify`.
> - ThreadLoop protocol, proof plan, and `session next` remain version `3`; SQLite schema remains version `6`.
> - The runner receives only:
>
>   ```text
>   repo_root
>   session_id
>   wake_id
>   mode: normal
>   ```
>
> - Use one unique `wake_id` per scheduled delivery. Reuse it only for an ambiguous duplicate delivery of that same wake.
> - Keep `.threadloop/state/`, receipt packages, wake handoffs, and the pilot report out of the feature diff unless explicitly selected as review evidence.
>
> ## Canonical Contracts
>
> ### Runner skill contract
>
> Each Codex wake:
>
> 1. Receives the four explicit inputs.
> 2. Validates the canonical repository root, named branch, HEAD, clean worktree, protocol version, explicit session, audit status, and repair budget.
> 3. Reads `session next`.
> 4. Performs at most one authorized action:
>    - one executable lifecycle transition;
>    - one bounded `COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION` or `COMMIT_REPAIR` action;
>    - one stored local gate; or
>    - no mutation and a handoff.
> 5. Stops after that action or handoff.
>
> The skill is the runner. No extracted TypeScript controller sits between Codex and the existing ThreadLoop CLI in this pilot.
>
> ### Operator-retained wake handoff
>
> Before a transition or other side effect, the operator retains the fields the skill requires:
>
> ```text
> repo_root
> session_id
> wake_id
> mode
> branch
> head_sha
> worktree_clean
> lifecycle_state
> lifecycle_state_version
> selected_action
> action_started
> action_outcome
> action_result
> transition_request
> stop_reason
> next_authority
> ```
>
> The record may be maintained as one append-only local JSONL file. It is needed for honest duplicate/crash handling, but it does not require new runtime code.
>
> ### Coding-agent action
>
> During `COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION`, Codex may:
>
> - Read the task, rules, and plan.
> - Write failing behavior tests.
> - Implement the smallest feature.
> - Run focused non-ThreadLoop checks.
> - Create at most one scoped commit.
>
> It must leave a clean worktree and stop. It must not run a ThreadLoop gate, transition, evidence import, push, or PR action in the same wake.
>
> `COMMIT_REPAIR` follows the same boundary and is limited to the complete current blocking finding set.
>
> ### External evidence handoff
>
> The runner stops when signed CI or review evidence is required. The operator:
>
> 1. Invokes the exact pinned caller workflow.
> 2. Downloads the exact package for the current feature HEAD.
> 3. Imports it using the explicit session.
> 4. Records the result in the wake handoff.
> 5. Starts a later wake with a new `wake_id`.
>
> These are supervised pilot operations, not runner behavior.
>
> ### Human stop
>
> At `ready_for_human`, `blocked`, `completed`, or exhausted repair budget, Codex starts no new action. The pilot ends at `ready_for_human` without approval or merge.
>
> ## TDD And BDD Implementation Strategy
>
> The feature wake begins with these red scenarios:
>
> 1. Authorized payment + new key -> one capture and one event.
> 2. Same key retry -> identical response and no second event.
> 3. Captured payment + new key -> conflict, no mutation, no event.
> 4. Pending payment + new key -> conflict, no mutation, no event.
> 5. Missing scope or idempotency key -> existing fail-closed behavior remains.
>
> Only after the targeted tests demonstrate the gap does Codex modify `src/signalpay_api/app.py`. It then reruns the focused tests and creates one feature commit.
>
> Full `make verify` is not bundled into the implementation action. ThreadLoop runs it later as the stored local gate while the repository is clean and committed.
>
> If review produces a legitimate blocker, a later repair wake begins from a test or reproduction for that finding, applies the smallest correction, and creates one repair commit. All local and signed evidence must then be refreshed for the repair HEAD.
>
> The pilot deliberately starts at least one verification, review, or repair wake in a fresh Codex context. The new context receives only the repository, the runner skill, and the four explicit inputs.
>
> ## Component Design
>
> The pilot uses the existing architecture:
>
> ```text
> operator or scheduled task
>   -> four explicit wake inputs
>   -> Codex reads runner skill
>   -> existing ThreadLoop CLI projection
>   -> one Codex action or one handoff
>   -> operator records outcome
>   -> later independent wake
> ```
>
> ThreadLoop owns lifecycle truth, proof plans, receipts, review evidence, repair budget, guarded transitions, and audit persistence.
>
> The runner skill owns the procedure for one wake. Codex owns the bounded code change. The operator owns wake delivery and the local handoff record. GitHub Actions owns signed sensor execution. The human owns irreversible authority.
>
> The pilot is testing whether this division is usable. Adding a software controller before running the pilot would hide the coordination friction the experiment needs to reveal.
>
> ## Failure And Recovery Rules
>
> - Missing or invalid wake input -> run no ThreadLoop command; operator corrects the invocation.
> - Dirty worktree before a wake -> preserve it exactly and stop; never clean, reset, stash, or repeat work automatically.
> - Branch, HEAD, repository, session, or protocol mismatch -> stop and record the observed facts.
> - Ambiguous transition response -> reuse the same wake ID and exact retained request only after revalidating the Git snapshot.
> - `STATE_VERSION_CONFLICT` or `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` -> stop; do not mint a new key in the same wake.
> - Crash during repository work -> preserve the worktree and mark the handoff outcome unknown; a human inspects before any later action.
> - Uncertain local gate outcome -> do not replay it as a duplicate.
> - Missing, stale, or corrupt proof -> remain in the current state and follow the exact required-work handoff.
> - Signed package collection/import failure -> retain the current lifecycle state and exact error; retry only under operator supervision.
> - Blocking review finding -> enter repair only through the executable reviewing-to-repairing transition and within budget.
> - Clean review -> do not invent a defect to exercise repair.
> - Fresh Codex context cannot continue -> record a failed usability criterion; do not compensate with hidden transcript context.
> - Unknown required-work code -> fail closed and hand it to the operator.
> - `ready_for_human`, blocked state, exhausted budget, approval, or merge requirement -> stop for human authority.
>
> ## Commit Plan
>
> ### ThreadLoop skill prerequisite
>
> 1. `feat(runner): add one-action wake contract and transition proof`
>    - Review the existing branch’s skill and its small ThreadLoop regression test together.
>    - The test remains internal and is not promoted to pilot code.
> 2. `docs(runner): document supervised consumer pilot boundary`
>    - Make explicit that the npm package contains the CLI, the skill is a repository procedure, and no scheduler/controller is included.
>
> If those commits are not merged before the pilot, pin the exact reviewed `dce6d423bd790258ec09f84e3115b38632da8d6d` snapshot and describe the pilot as pre-merge validation.
>
> ### SignalPay pilot
>
> 1. `chore(threadloop): add pinned supervised pilot enablement`
>    - Add the exact skill snapshot, pinned sensor caller workflow, ThreadLoop config, and pilot plan.
> 2. `feat(payments): enforce safe capture transitions`
>    - Keep the red tests and smallest implementation in one behavior-closed commit.
> 3. `fix(payments): address current review findings`
>    - Add only when a legitimate current blocking review requires repair.
>
> ## Branch And PR Flow
>
> 1. Review the exact ThreadLoop runner-skill branch against current `origin/main`.
> 2. Either merge a new/reopened runner-skill PR or explicitly pin the reviewed branch SHA for a pre-merge pilot. Do not imply the closed PR is merged.
> 3. Build and verify the ThreadLoop CLI tarball from that exact SHA.
> 4. Create a fresh SignalPay worktree and feature branch from `a6e832cd8a5e031a3ea65729e04f1406ccf59b88`.
> 5. Add and commit the minimal pilot enablement.
> 6. Start the explicit ThreadLoop session and retain its `session_id`.
> 7. Invoke serialized Codex wakes manually or through a simple scheduled task, using the skill and four explicit inputs.
> 8. After the implementation commit, let ThreadLoop run `make verify` in a later wake.
> 9. Under explicit pilot execution authority, the operator may push and open the SignalPay feature PR, invoke the signed sensors, and import their packages. The runner never performs those operations.
> 10. Follow current review evidence through optional repair and fresh proof.
> 11. Stop at `ready_for_human`, verify/export the audit, and write the pilot report.
> 12. Decide from measured friction whether a separate controller/scheduler ticket is warranted.
>
> Before either PR, pin one fixed point and review the complete change set, including untracked files:
>
> - Run the Codex `code-review` skill on separate Standards and Spec axes.
> - Run this independent read-only review against the same fixed point:
>
>   ```bash
>   claude -p \
>     --model claude-sonnet-5 \
>     --effort high \
>     --permission-mode plan \
>     "<focused prompt forbidding edits, network, subagents, and a full test run; require confirmed P0-P3 findings with file, line, evidence, and correction, or CLEAN>"
>   ```
>
> Reproduce and deduplicate findings, resolve every confirmed actionable issue, rerun affected and full checks, then rerun both reviews before opening the PR. Do not silently substitute another Claude model.
>
> ## Test Plan
>
> ### ThreadLoop prerequisite verification
>
> ```bash
> npx vitest run tests/integration/runner-replay.test.ts
> npm run check
> npm run security:dependencies
> git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
> ```
>
> This verifies the existing runner-skill change inside ThreadLoop. It does not make the test part of SignalPay or the live pilot runtime.
>
> ### SignalPay feature verification
>
> ```bash
> uv run pytest tests/test_payments_api.py -q
> make verify
> git diff --check <pilot-fixed-point>...HEAD
> ```
>
> Required live acceptance:
>
> - The feature tests pass at the feature HEAD.
> - The ThreadLoop local gate receipt is current.
> - The signed CI package is produced by the pinned workflow and imported.
> - The current signed review package is imported.
> - Any legitimate repair produces a descendant commit and fresh proof.
> - A fresh Codex context completes at least one later wake.
> - Final state is `ready_for_human`.
> - Audit verification and export pass.
> - No runner-owned push, PR, approval, merge, deployment, publication, secret rotation, or policy activation occurs.
>
> ### Review commands
>
> Use the same fixed point for Codex and Claude:
>
> ```bash
> claude -p \
>   --model claude-sonnet-5 \
>   --effort high \
>   --permission-mode plan \
>   "<read the applicable AGENTS.md, rules, feature specification, and complete fixed-point diff; do not edit, use network, spawn subagents, or run the full suite; report confirmed P0-P3 findings with file, line, evidence, and correction, or CLEAN>"
> ```
>
> After remediation, rerun the focused tests, `make verify`, both reviews, and the fixed-point diff check.
>
> ### Usability measurements
>
> Record:
>
> - Setup time before the first Codex wake.
> - Total wake count.
> - Operator and human interventions.
> - Time spent retaining handoffs and collecting/importing evidence.
> - Ambiguous or unknown stops.
> - Dirty-worktree or crash recovery.
> - Fresh-context continuation success.
> - Whether one implementation wake and commit was natural for the feature.
> - Any attempted authority violation or duplicate effect.
>
> ## Definition Of Done
>
> - The reviewed runner skill is available in the fresh SignalPay worktree.
> - No replay test, fixture, or extracted controller code is a SignalPay dependency.
> - The pilot uses the existing ThreadLoop CLI and explicit four-input wakes.
> - Every wake has a retained handoff with no more than one started action.
> - Codex implements the capture-state feature from red tests to one clean, scoped feature commit.
> - Existing capture, auth, idempotency, response, and event contracts remain passing.
> - A fresh Codex context continues at least one later wake without transcript reconstruction.
> - Current local, signed CI, and signed review evidence is imported for the actual feature HEAD.
> - Any real blocking review finding is repaired within budget and reverified.
> - ThreadLoop reaches and stops at `ready_for_human`.
> - Audit verification/export reconstructs the lifecycle and authority handoffs.
> - The pilot report records technical evidence and manual coordination cost.
> - No scheduler, controller, queue, lease, provider abstraction, dashboard, or hosted service is added.
> - Any future automation build is justified by observed pilot friction rather than assumed need.
>
> ## Assumptions And Defaults
>
> - The runner skill is sufficient for a supervised pilot because Codex and the operator can execute its documented procedure directly.
> - “Sufficient” does not mean self-scheduling: a human or simple scheduled task still supplies the next wake.
> - The operator-retained JSONL handoff is operational evidence, not product code.
> - SignalPay is the default consumer because it has repo-local rules, TDD guidance, `make verify`, GitHub CI, and a bounded payment mutation surface.
> - Capture-state safety is the default fresh feature because it is absent from SignalPay `main` and does not duplicate the open refund PR.
> - The exact feature behavior should be approved before binding the immutable proof plan.
> - The current `runner-replay.test.ts` may remain as ThreadLoop regression coverage. The historical large replay is irrelevant to this plan.

# Lifecycle Observation: Pre-PR Local Iteration

## Status

Observed during the supervised SignalPay consumer pilot on 2026-07-30.
Documented only; no ThreadLoop lifecycle, runner, schema, CLI, or SignalPay
source change is authorized by this observation.

## User Need

A ThreadLoop user must be able to make as many task-scoped local modifications
as necessary before opening a pull request. This includes responding to local
tests, standards checks, specification review, and other pre-PR evidence.

The number of local iterations is not known when the session begins. The
governance boundary should constrain the scope and effects of each wake, not
assume that one implementation commit is sufficient.

## Observed Current Flow

```text
implementing
  -> COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION
  -> verifying
  -> local and signed CI proof
  -> reviewing
  -> signed PR review
  -> optional repairing
```

The runner allows one clean, scoped commit during a bounded repository-work
wake. That is a useful per-wake invariant. In the observed flow, however,
`COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION` is available only before verification, while
`COMMIT_REPAIR` is tied to the signed-review repair cycle. Once the pilot
entered `verifying`, a confirmed pre-PR finding had no authorized path back to
local repository work.

## Missing Capability

ThreadLoop needs a governed pre-PR iteration loop with these properties:

1. A session may authorize multiple local repository-work wakes before a PR.
2. Every wake still performs at most one action.
3. Every repository-work wake remains task-scoped, runs focused checks, creates
   at most one scoped commit, leaves a clean worktree, and stops.
4. A changed `HEAD` makes earlier local or signed proof stale and requires fresh
   proof.
5. Local findings can trigger another implementation iteration without
   pretending that signed PR review already exists.
6. The post-PR signed-review repair budget and repair authority remain distinct.
7. The runner still cannot push, open a PR, approve, merge, deploy, publish,
   activate policy, or recover a blocked session.

## State-Model Questions

This pilot does not prescribe a solution. The follow-up design should compare
at least these possibilities:

- Keep `implementing` repeatable until an explicit pre-PR fixed-point
  transition.
- Add a distinct local-review or local-iteration state.
- Allow a guarded `verifying -> implementing` transition when the PR has not
  been opened and current local review identifies task-scoped work.

For each option, define:

- the canonical source of local finding authority;
- allowed positive and negative transitions;
- proof-staleness behavior after every new commit;
- idempotency and crash recovery for repeated wakes;
- the relationship to the existing repair budget;
- how `session next` distinguishes pre-PR iteration from post-PR repair; and
- operator-facing recovery instructions.

## Pilot Evidence

- Session: `session_535fdfc6-b4bd-4b14-a512-d250c7b07b06`
- State: `verifying`, version 4
- HEAD: `2efaa06873843ad3af0fdf8b07c625a3af8893ed`
- Local gate receipt:
  `receipt_fc711340-bc15-40c6-ba11-d7f5386a1707`
- Confirmed pre-PR finding: capture authentication rejection tests do not yet
  prove the full no-mutation contract.
- Worktree status when documented: clean
- Override taken: none
- Draft PR opened: no
- Out-of-band repository commit: no

## Pilot Decision

Preserve the current state and evidence exactly. Do not work around the
lifecycle. Treat the blocked pre-PR iteration as measured DX and workflow
evidence for a separately reviewed lifecycle-design change.

Main is rebased at `6a59de9` (I see #74 also landed, restructuring the runner skill). Here's the situation.

## The pilot's own finding got fixed, and Attempt 1 is resumable

The deadlock was: `verifying` + passing gate + a confirmed pre-PR finding, with no authorized way back to local work. The transition table now reads:

```
VERIFYING        → [IMPLEMENTING, PRE_PR_REVIEWING, REVIEWING, REPAIRING]
PRE_PR_REVIEWING → [IMPLEMENTING, REVIEWING]
```

I checked all seven properties `lifecycle-observation.md` demanded against the shipped code — multiple pre-PR wakes, one action per wake, HEAD-bound proof staleness, local findings without faking signed review, repair budget kept distinct, runner still barred from push/PR. All present. The shipped design took *two* of your three candidate options together: a distinct `pre_pr_reviewing` state **and** a guarded `verifying → implementing`, plus a `PRE_PR_REVIEW_BOUNDARY_REQUIRED` guard forcing the boundary before `reviewing`.

More directly: I asked the stuck session what it can do now (read-only — I checksummed the DB before and after, unchanged, and kept a backup):

```
phase: pre_pr        contract_status: migration_required     repair_budget: limit 3
required_work: [{ code: "MIGRATE_SESSION_SCHEMA",
                  description: "Run `threadloop init`, then rerun `threadloop session next`",
                  owner_issue: 69 }]
```

It correctly derives `phase: pre_pr` from a v6 database and hands you a migration path citing issue #69 — the issue this pilot generated. **The earlier recommendation to restart as Attempt 2 is no longer the best option.**

## What's stale in the plan

| Plan says | Actually now |
|---|---|
| ThreadLoop main `1312105` | `6a59de9` |
| Pin unmerged `dce6d42`, "pre-merge validation" | Runner skill **merged**, restructured by #74 |
| protocol/proof/session-next **3**, schema **6** | protocol **4**, sessionNext **4**, proofPlan 3, handoff 3, schema **7** |
| "one clean, scoped feature commit" | Now multiple scoped commits across pre-PR wakes |
| No migration recovery rule | `MIGRATE_SESSION_SCHEMA` is a live path this pilot will use |

The four wake inputs are unchanged. SignalPay baseline `a6e832c` is still `origin/main` (though there are four open PRs now, not just #4). Two things in the pilot worktree need refreshing either way: the sensor workflows are pinned to the unmerged `dce6d42`, and the installed skill snapshot predates #74.

## What I'd do

Resume Attempt 1: `threadloop init` to migrate, then use pre-PR iteration wakes to fix the P2 (test-only — no-mutation assertions on the `403` capture path plus a wrong-audience `POST /capture`), re-verify, pass the `pre_pr_reviewing` boundary, and only then push. That produces one continuous audit ledger containing both the deadlock and the recovery, and it exercises the v6→v7 migration against a *real* legacy session with real history — something the synthetic test fixtures can't fully substitute for.

The honest tradeoff: it makes the ledger messier as a demo (a mid-session schema migration), and the migration is one-way. A fresh Attempt 2 gives a pristine single-version run but never reproduces the bug you fixed.

### 1. Validate inputs

Validate all four inputs before any ThreadLoop command. Require `repo_root` to be an existing absolute directory whose
bytes equal its filesystem `realpath`. Reject `~`, relative paths, and symlink aliases. Pass each input as one exact
argument; do not construct an interpolated shell command.

### 2. Snapshot Git

Run only these read-only observations with the explicit root:

```text
git -C <repo_root> rev-parse --show-toplevel
git -C <repo_root> symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD
git -C <repo_root> rev-parse --verify --end-of-options HEAD^{commit}
git -C <repo_root> --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all --ignore-submodules=none
git -C <repo_root> worktree list --porcelain
```

Require an exact root and worktree entry, a named branch, a commit HEAD, and an empty status. Retain
`(repo_root, branch, head_sha, clean=true)`. Preserve and stop on any mismatch; do not repair the checkout.

### 3. Verify protocol v4

Run `threadloop protocol --json` from exactly `repo_root`. Require:

```text
ok = true
command = "protocol"
data.contractVersions.protocol = 4
data.contractVersions.proofPlan = 3
data.contractVersions.sessionNext = 4
data.contractVersions.handoff = 3
```

Unknown, missing, differently typed, or different versions fail closed.

### 4. Use the migration-safe read first

Run:

```text
threadloop session next --session <session_id> --json
```

Require `ok: true`, `command: "session next"`, `data.contract_version: 4`, and an exact session id. Before any normal
session read, require:

```text
data.lifecycle.storage_schema_version = 7
data.lifecycle.contract_status = "current"
```

Stop when the lifecycle contract or any proof, staleness, repair-budget, or audit status is `migration_required`.
`SESSION_SCHEMA_MIGRATION_REQUIRED -> MIGRATE_SESSION_SCHEMA` is a recognized external-operator handoff. The runner must
not invoke `threadloop init` or otherwise migrate the repository.

### 5. Validate session status

Run `threadloop session status --session <session_id> --json`. Require exact session id, a non-null task, matching task
id, non-empty title and goal, string-or-null issue reference, known task state, and non-negative safe state version.
These task fields define repository-work scope. Stored session Git fields are not live Git authority.

### 6. Validate a fresh session-next v4 projection

Run session next again and require it to match the retained session and Git snapshots. Validate:

- lifecycle state/version match session status;
- `lifecycle.phase` is `pre_pr` or `post_pr`;
- schema is `7` and contract status is `current`;
- candidate is null or has known source/target, matching source/version, and boolean `executable`;
- repository branch, HEAD, and clean status exactly match the Git snapshot;
- repair limit is `3` and status, counts, remaining count, and exhausted flag agree;
- `pre_pr_review.status`, implementation basis, proof, CI, signed review, staleness, and audit values are known;
- audit status is `valid`; and
- guard and work arrays are both empty or contain one known matching pair.

Lifecycle states:

```text
queued
framed
proof_ready
implementing
verifying
pre_pr_reviewing
reviewing
repairing
ready_for_human
blocked
completed
```

Status allowlists:

- `proof.status` and gate statuses: `missing`, `passed`, `failed`, `stale`, `corrupt`; top-level proof also permits
  `migration_required`;
- `ci_proof.status`: `policy_missing`, `missing`, `passed`, `stale`, `corrupt`;
- `review.status`: `policy_missing`, `missing`, `current`, `stale`, `corrupt`;
- `pre_pr_review.status`: `not_started`, `review_required`, `changes_required`, `cleared`, `stale`,
  `migration_required`;
- `staleness.status`: `current`, `missing`, `stale`, `corrupt`, `migration_required`;
- `repair_budget.status`: `available`, `exhausted`, `migration_required`;
- `audit.status`: `valid`, `corrupt`, `migration_required`.

Known guard/work pairs include:

```text
BLOCKED_PRIOR_STATE_REQUIRED -> RESTORE_BLOCKED_PRIOR_STATE

input.content:
# ThreadLoop Consumer Pilot: Capture-State Safety (Attempt 2)

## Purpose

Answer one acceptance question with a real consumer-repository run:

> Can a coding agent use the ThreadLoop runner skill to implement a fresh SignalPay feature across
> separate wakes, preserve lifecycle and proof state, iterate locally before a pull request, respond to
> current review evidence, and stop at `ready_for_human`?

This is Attempt 2. Attempt 1 reached `verifying` and stopped at a genuine lifecycle deadlock: a confirmed
pre-PR review finding had no authorized path back to local repository work. That deadlock is the reason
ThreadLoop issue #69 exists. Attempt 2 runs against the lifecycle that closed it.

Attempt 1 evidence is retained unchanged and is not superseded by this run.

## Pinned fixed points

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ThreadLoop source | `6a59de94a354a4b0584e34cf98bfe5f4fc38a15f` (merged `main`) |
| ThreadLoop package SHA-256 | `8c0b61092ab8cd29fb79d901fb1e55e44970f934d651287c0fcfb686d55f8222` |
| Runner skill SHA-256 | `77d73d15555e9e2bf4df77f3275d5e7bb137103493d7fadb6469e6560d7de34b` |
| SignalPay baseline | `a6e832cd8a5e031a3ea65729e04f1406ccf59b88` |
| Pilot branch | `feat/threadloop-capture-state-pilot-2` |

Contract versions this pilot binds: protocol `4`, `sessionNext` `4`, `proofPlan` `3`, `handoff` `3`,
storage schema `7`.

The runner skill is now merged, so this pilot uses a reviewed commit on `main` rather than the pre-merge
snapshot Attempt 1 had to pin. Both reusable sensor workflows are pinned to the same ThreadLoop SHA.

## Feature: capture-state safety and retry semantics

Governing rules: `PAY-010` (new transitions explicit and tested), `PAY-002` (auth and scope checked
before mutation, proven by no-mutation assertions), `PAY-004` (retry returns the original response and
emits no duplicate event), `PAY-001`, `PAY-003`, `PAY-005`, `PAY-006`, `PAY-007`.

Required behavior:

1. Only an `authorized` payment may begin a new capture.
2. An exact idempotent retry of a successful capture returns the original response and emits no second
   event.
3. A new idempotency key against a `captured` payment fails without mutating payment state, events, or
   idempotency results.
4. A new idempotency key against a `pending` payment fails the same way.
5. Existing auth, scope, camelCase response, and event contracts stay stable.

### Failure-path coverage carried forward from Attempt 1

Attempt 1's pre-PR review confirmed one P2 on two independent axes: capture auth rejection was not proven
to be side-effect free. `PAY-002` requires that assertion and `PAY-007` requires failure-path coverage.
Attempt 2 includes it in the planned behavior rather than discovering it at the review gate:

- the insufficient-scope `403` capture path asserts unchanged payment, events, and idempotency results;
- a wrong-audience `POST /payments/{id}/capture` case asserts the same.

## Authority boundary

ThreadLoop owns lifecycle truth, proof plans, receipts, review evidence, repair budget, guarded
transitions, and audit persistence.

The runner skill owns the procedure for one wake and performs at most one action per wake. It may never
push, open or merge a pull request, approve, deploy, publish, rotate secrets, activate policy, recover a
blocked session, or run `threadloop init`.

The operator owns wake delivery, the retained wake record, schema migration, proof-plan binding, pre-PR
review outcome recording, push, sensor invocation, evidence import, and pull-request creation.

The human owns approval, merge, and policy authority. The pilot stops at `ready_for_human`.

## Pre-PR iteration (new in Attempt 2)

The lifecycle now permits:

```text
verifying        -> implementing | pre_pr_reviewing | reviewing | repairing
pre_pr_reviewing -> implementing | reviewing
```

Consequences for this pilot:

- `COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION` may recur across any number of serialized pre-PR `implementing` wakes, so the
  feature is no longer required to land in exactly one commit.
- A pre-PR finding is recorded through `RECORD_PRE_PR_REVIEW_OUTCOME`, which carries non-empty input and
  is therefore an operator action, not a runner-synthesized transition.
- `PRE_PR_REVIEW_BOUNDARY_REQUIRED` forces the session through `pre_pr_reviewing` before `reviewing`, so
  the pre-PR gate cannot be skipped by going straight to a pull request.
- Pre-PR iteration must not consume repair budget. The budget limit is `3` and must still read `3`
  remaining when the pilot reaches `reviewing`.
- Any new commit invalidates prior local and signed proof for the old HEAD; fresh proof is required.

## Definition of done

- The merged runner skill governs every wake; no replay test, fixture, or extracted controller is a
  SignalPay dependency.
- Every wake has a retained record and starts at most one action.
- The capture-state feature is implemented from red tests, across as many pre-PR `implementing` wakes as
  the work needs.
- Existing capture, auth, idempotency, response, and event contracts still pass.
- At least one later wake runs in a genuinely fresh agent context with no transcript inheritance.
- Both independent pre-PR reviews are clean at a pinned fixed point before any push.
- The session passes through `pre_pr_reviewing` before `reviewing`.
- Repair budget reads 3 of 3 remaining on entry to `reviewing`, proving pre-PR iteration consumed none.
- Current local, signed CI, and signed review evidence is imported for the actual feature HEAD.
- Any genuine post-PR blocking finding is repaired within budget and reverified.
- The session reaches and stops at `ready_for_human`.
- Audit verification and export reconstruct the lifecycle and authority handoffs.
- The pilot report records technical evidence, manual coordination cost, and a comparison with Attempt 1.
- No scheduler, controller, queue, lease, provider abstraction, dashboard, or hosted service is added.

## Out of scope

Extracting anything from `runner-replay.test.ts`; changing ThreadLoop lifecycle, schema, protocol, CLI, or
runtime; touching SignalPay PRs #1, #2, #4, or #7; runner-owned push, PR, approval, merge, deploy,
publish, secret rotation, or policy activation; manufacturing a review defect to force a repair cycle;
same-checkout multi-agent execution; modifying Attempt 1's worktree, branch, or session.

## Recovery rules

- Missing or invalid wake input: run no ThreadLoop command; the operator corrects the invocation.
- Dirty worktree: preserve exactly and stop. Never clean, reset, stash, or discard.
- Root, branch, HEAD, session, or protocol mismatch: stop and record observed facts.
- `SESSION_SCHEMA_MIGRATION_REQUIRED -> MIGRATE_SESSION_SCHEMA`: operator runs `threadloop init`, then
  rereads `session next`. The runner must not migrate.
- Ambiguous transition: retry only the byte-identical retained request after revalidating the Git
  snapshot. Never mint a new idempotency key in the same wake.
- `STATE_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, `TRANSITION_GUARD_FAILED`, `STATE_CORRUPTED`: stop.
- Repository or gate action: never replayed.
- Crash during repository work: preserve the worktree, mark the outcome unknown, hand to a human.
- Missing, stale, or corrupt proof: stay in the current state and follow the exact required-work handoff.
- Blocking review finding: enter repair only through the executable reviewing-to-repairing transition and
  within budget.
- Clean review: do not invent a defect to exercise repair.
- Fresh-context wake cannot continue: record a failed usability criterion; do not supply hidden context.
- Unknown required-work code: fail closed and hand to the operator.

# ThreadLoop Consumer Pilot: Capture-State Safety (Attempt 2)

## Purpose

Answer one acceptance question with a real consumer-repository run:

> Can a coding agent use the ThreadLoop runner skill to implement a fresh SignalPay feature across
> separate wakes, preserve lifecycle and proof state, iterate locally before a pull request, respond to
> current review evidence, and stop at `ready_for_human`?

This is Attempt 2. Attempt 1 reached `verifying` and stopped at a genuine lifecycle deadlock: a confirmed
pre-PR review finding had no authorized path back to local repository work. That deadlock is the reason
ThreadLoop issue #69 exists. Attempt 2 runs against the lifecycle that closed it.

Attempt 1 evidence is retained unchanged and is not superseded by this run.

## Pinned fixed points

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ThreadLoop source | `6a59de94a354a4b0584e34cf98bfe5f4fc38a15f` (merged `main`) |
| ThreadLoop package SHA-256 | `8c0b61092ab8cd29fb79d901fb1e55e44970f934d651287c0fcfb686d55f8222` |
| Runner skill SHA-256 | `77d73d15555e9e2bf4df77f3275d5e7bb137103493d7fadb6469e6560d7de34b` |
| SignalPay baseline | `a6e832cd8a5e031a3ea65729e04f1406ccf59b88` |
| Pilot branch | `feat/threadloop-capture-state-pilot-2` |

Contract versions this pilot binds: protocol `4`, `sessionNext` `4`, `proofPlan` `3`, `handoff` `3`,
storage schema `7`.

The runner skill is now merged, so this pilot uses a reviewed commit on `main` rather than the pre-merge
snapshot Attempt 1 had to pin. Both reusable sensor workflows are pinned to the same ThreadLoop SHA.

## Feature: capture-state safety and retry semantics

Governing rules: `PAY-010` (new transitions explicit and tested), `PAY-002` (auth and scope checked
before mutation, proven by no-mutation assertions), `PAY-004` (retry returns the original response and
emits no duplicate event), `PAY-001`, `PAY-003`, `PAY-005`, `PAY-006`, `PAY-007`.

Required behavior:

1. Only an `authorized` payment may begin a new capture.
2. An exact idempotent retry of a successful capture returns the original response and emits no second
   event.
3. A new idempotency key against a `captured` payment fails without mutating payment state, events, or
   idempotency results.
4. A new idempotency key against a `pending` payment fails the same way.
5. Existing auth, scope, camelCase response, and event contracts stay stable.

### Failure-path coverage carried forward from Attempt 1

Attempt 1's pre-PR review confirmed one P2 on two independent axes: capture auth rejection was not proven
to be side-effect free. `PAY-002` requires that assertion and `PAY-007` requires failure-path coverage.
Attempt 2 includes it in the planned behavior rather than discovering it at the review gate:

- the insufficient-scope `403` capture path asserts unchanged payment, events, and idempotency results;
- a wrong-audience `POST /payments/{id}/capture` case asserts the same.

## Authority boundary

ThreadLoop owns lifecycle truth, proof plans, receipts, review evidence, repair budget, guarded
transitions, and audit persistence.

The runner skill owns the procedure for one wake and performs at most one action per wake. It may never
push, open or merge a pull request, approve, deploy, publish, rotate secrets, activate policy, recover a
blocked session, or run `threadloop init`.

The operator owns wake delivery, the retained wake record, schema migration, proof-plan binding, pre-PR
review outcome recording, push, sensor invocation, evidence import, and pull-request creation.

The human owns approval, merge, and policy authority. The pilot stops at `ready_for_human`.

## Pre-PR iteration (new in Attempt 2)

The lifecycle now permits:

```text
verifying        -> implementing | pre_pr_reviewing | reviewing | repairing
pre_pr_reviewing -> implementing | reviewing
```

Consequences for this pilot:

- `COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION` may recur across any number of serialized pre-PR `implementing` wakes, so the
  feature is no longer required to land in exactly one commit.
- A pre-PR finding is recorded through `RECORD_PRE_PR_REVIEW_OUTCOME`, which carries non-empty input and
  is therefore an operator action, not a runner-synthesized transition.
- `PRE_PR_REVIEW_BOUNDARY_REQUIRED` forces the session through `pre_pr_reviewing` before `reviewing`, so
  the pre-PR gate cannot be skipped by going straight to a pull request.
- Pre-PR iteration must not consume repair budget. The budget limit is `3` and must still read `3`
  remaining when the pilot reaches `reviewing`.
- Any new commit invalidates prior local and signed proof for the old HEAD; fresh proof is required.

## Definition of done

- The merged runner skill governs every wake; no replay test, fixture, or extracted controller is a
  SignalPay dependency.
- Every wake has a retained record and starts at most one action.
- The capture-state feature is implemented from red tests, across as many pre-PR `implementing` wakes as
  the work needs.
- Existing capture, auth, idempotency, response, and event contracts still pass.
- At least one later wake runs in a genuinely fresh agent context with no transcript inheritance.
- Both independent pre-PR reviews are clean at a pinned fixed point before any push.
- The session passes through `pre_pr_reviewing` before `reviewing`.
- Repair budget reads 3 of 3 remaining on entry to `reviewing`, proving pre-PR iteration consumed none.
- Current local, signed CI, and signed review evidence is imported for the actual feature HEAD.
- Any genuine post-PR blocking finding is repaired within budget and reverified.
- The session reaches and stops at `ready_for_human`.
- Audit verification and export reconstruct the lifecycle and authority handoffs.
- The pilot report records technical evidence, manual coordination cost, and a comparison with Attempt 1.
- No scheduler, controller, queue, lease, provider abstraction, dashboard, or hosted service is added.

## Out of scope

Extracting anything from `runner-replay.test.ts`; changing ThreadLoop lifecycle, schema, protocol, CLI, or
runtime; touching SignalPay PRs #1, #2, #4, or #7; runner-owned push, PR, approval, merge, deploy,
publish, secret rotation, or policy activation; manufacturing a review defect to force a repair cycle;
same-checkout multi-agent execution; modifying Attempt 1's worktree, branch, or session.

## Recovery rules

- Missing or invalid wake input: run no ThreadLoop command; the operator corrects the invocation.
- Dirty worktree: preserve exactly and stop. Never clean, reset, stash, or discard.
- Root, branch, HEAD, session, or protocol mismatch: stop and record observed facts.
- `SESSION_SCHEMA_MIGRATION_REQUIRED -> MIGRATE_SESSION_SCHEMA`: operator runs `threadloop init`, then
  rereads `session next`. The runner must not migrate.
- Ambiguous transition: retry only the byte-identical retained request after revalidating the Git
  snapshot. Never mint a new idempotency key in the same wake.
- `STATE_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, `TRANSITION_GUARD_FAILED`, `STATE_CORRUPTED`: stop.
- Repository or gate action: never replayed.
- Crash during repository work: preserve the worktree, mark the outcome unknown, hand to a human.
- Missing, stale, or corrupt proof: stay in the current state and follow the exact required-work handoff.
- Blocking review finding: enter repair only through the executable reviewing-to-repairing transition and
  within budget.
- Clean review: do not invent a defect to exercise repair.
- Fresh-context wake cannot continue: record a failed usability criterion; do not supply hidden context.
- Unknown required-work code: fail closed and hand to the operator.
- `ready_for_human`, `blocked`, `completed`, or exhausted budget: stop for human authority.

| 2 | operator | `framed -> proof_ready`, binding the immutable proof plan | proof plan |
| 3 | runner wake | `proof_ready -> implementing` | `{}` |
| 4 | runner wake | `COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION` — red tests, smallest change, one scoped commit | repository work |
| 5 | runner wake | `implementing -> verifying` | `{}` |
| 6 | runner wake | run the declared `make-verify` gate | gate |
| 7 | operator | pre-PR reviews at a pinned fixed point (both axes, read-only) | — |
| 8 | operator | `RECORD_PRE_PR_REVIEW_OUTCOME` | review outcome |

| 11 | operator | `-> reviewing`; open the pull request; invoke the review sensor; import signed review | — |
| 12 | runner wake | `COMMIT_REPAIR` only if a genuine post-PR blocking finding exists, within budget | repository work |
| 13 | runner wake | `reviewing -> ready_for_human` | `{}` |
| 14 | operator | verify and export the audit; write the pilot report | — |

Steps 4 through 9 are the loop Attempt 1 could not perform. Each iteration produces its own scoped commit
and invalidates proof for the previous HEAD.

## Wake identity

One unique `wake_id` per delivery, matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`. Reuse an id only to retry an
ambiguous duplicate delivery of that same wake, and only with the byte-identical retained request. The
transition idempotency key is always `runner:v1:<wake_id>:<expected_state_version>`.

Before any action starts, retain the record fields listed in
`.agents/skills/threadloop-runner/references/wake-record.md`, keyed by
`(repo_root, session_id, wake_id)`, with `action_started` written before invocation.

## Fresh-context requirement

At least one wake at step 6 or later runs in a genuinely cold process that receives only the repository
path, the runner skill, and the four wake inputs. No transcript, no prior-wake summary, no inferred
session id. If it cannot continue, that is a recorded usability failure and must not be patched by
supplying context.

## TDD order for step 4

Red first, in `tests/test_payments_api.py`:

1. authorized payment + new key -> one capture, one event;
2. same key retry -> identical response, no second event;
3. `captured` payment + new key -> conflict, no mutation, no event, no idempotency result;
4. `pending` payment + new key -> conflict, same assertions;
5. insufficient scope on capture -> `403` and no payment, event, or idempotency change;
6. wrong audience on capture -> `401` and the same no-mutation assertions.

Cases 5 and 6 are the coverage Attempt 1's review flagged as P2. Only after these fail for the right
reason does `src/signalpay_api/app.py` change.

`make verify` is not run inside the implementation wake. ThreadLoop runs it as the declared gate at
step 6, against a clean committed tree.

## Evidence retained outside the worktree

Under `~/Code/threadloop-pilot-artifacts/signalpay-capture-state-attempt2/`:

- `wake-handoffs.jsonl` — one append-only record per wake;
- `retained-wake-requests/` — the exact request retained before each action;
- `receipts/` — downloaded signed packages;
- `review-ledger.md` — every pre-PR and post-PR finding with provenance and disposition;
- `threadloop-audit.jsonl` — verified audit export;
- `pilot-report.md` — measurements, friction, and the Attempt 1 comparison.

Keep `.threadloop/state/`, receipt packages, wake records, and the pilot report out of the feature diff.

from __future__ import annotations

from copy import deepcopy
from typing import Annotated, Any

from fastapi import FastAPI, Header, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from signalpay_api.contracts import PaymentStatus, build_payment_event, verify_session


class Payment(BaseModel):
    payment_id: str = Field(alias="paymentId")
    customer_id: str = Field(alias="customerId")
    amount: int
    currency: str
    status: PaymentStatus

    model_config = {"populate_by_name": True}


# PAY-010: capture is authorized -> captured. Every other current status is a
# rejected transition, not a silent re-capture.
CAPTURABLE_STATUS = "authorized"

INITIAL_PAYMENTS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    "pay_1001": {
        "paymentId": "pay_1001",
        "customerId": "cus_9001",
        "amount": 12500,
        "currency": "USD",
        "status": "authorized",
    },
    "pay_1002": {
        "paymentId": "pay_1002",
        "customerId": "cus_9002",
        "amount": 4900,
        "currency": "USD",
        "status": "pending",
    },
}

payments: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = deepcopy(INITIAL_PAYMENTS)
payment_events: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
idempotency_results: dict[tuple[str, str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}

app = FastAPI(
    title="SignalPay Payments API",
    summary="Self-contained payments API for the Qodo quality-first workshop.",
    description=(
        "Use this API through `/docs` to practice planning, Qodo rules, "
        "local verification gates, PR review, and remediation."
    ),
)


def reset_state() -> None:
    """Reset in-memory state for tests and local workshop retries."""
    payments.clear()
    payments.update(deepcopy(INITIAL_PAYMENTS))
    payment_events.clear()
    idempotency_results.clear()


def require_principal(
    authorization: str | None,
    *,
    required_scope: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    if not authorization or not authorization.startswith("Bearer "):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Bearer session token is required")

    token = authorization.removeprefix("Bearer ").strip()
    try:
        principal = verify_session(token, "payments-api")
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail=str(exc)) from exc

    if required_scope and required_scope not in principal.scopes:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403,
            detail=f"{required_scope} scope is required",
        )


@app.get("/payments/{payment_id}", response_model=Payment, response_model_by_alias=True)
def get_payment(
    payment_id: str,
    authorization: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="Authorization")] = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require_principal(authorization)
    if payment_id not in payments:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="payment not found")
    return payments[payment_id]


@app.post("/payments/{payment_id}/capture", response_model=Payment, response_model_by_alias=True)
def capture_payment(
    payment_id: str,
    authorization: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="Authorization")] = None,
    idempotency_key: Annotated[
        str | None,
        Header(alias="Idempotency-Key"),
    ] = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require_principal(authorization, required_scope="payments:capture")
    if not idempotency_key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Idempotency-Key header is required")
    if payment_id not in payments:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="payment not found")

    result_key = ("capture", payment_id, idempotency_key)
    if result_key in idempotency_results:
        return idempotency_results[result_key]

    payment = payments[payment_id]
    payment["status"] = "captured"

    event = build_payment_event(
        event_type="payment.captured",
        payment_id=payment["paymentId"],
        customer_id=payment["customerId"],
        amount=payment["amount"],
        currency=payment["currency"],
        status="captured",
    )
    payment_events.append(dict(event))
    idempotency_results[result_key] = deepcopy(payment)
    return payment

# Attempt 2 Developer-Experience Findings

## DX-1 (blocking): signed evidence requires the caller workflow on the default branch

**Observed at:** the first signed-CI collection, with the session at `verifying` v4, local proof passed,
and both pre-PR reviews clean.

**Command and result:**

```text
gh workflow run threadloop.yml --ref feat/threadloop-capture-state-pilot-2 -f evidence=gate ...
HTTP 404: workflow threadloop.yml not found on the default branch
```

**Facts:**

- SignalPay default branch: `main`.
- `.github/workflows/threadloop.yml` exists on `feat/threadloop-capture-state-pilot-2` only.
- `gh workflow list` registers exactly one workflow, `Verify` (`verify.yml`), which is on `main`.
- GitHub resolves `workflow_dispatch` targets from the default branch. A `--ref` selects which ref the run
  checks out, but it cannot introduce a workflow that the default branch does not have.

**Consequence for adopters:** a consumer repository cannot produce signed ThreadLoop evidence for its
*first* governed feature branch. The pinned caller workflow must already be on the default branch. So
enabling ThreadLoop requires a preparatory change to the default branch before the first governed feature
run, and that preparatory change cannot itself be governed by signed evidence.

**Why the pilot did not predict this:** the build plan treats "invoke the exact pinned caller workflow" as
a single operator step and assumes dispatch succeeds. Attempt 1 stopped at the pre-PR lifecycle deadlock
and never reached signed-CI collection, so this constraint was undiscovered until now.

**Candidate remedies, not selected here:**

- Document a required one-time enablement change to the consumer's default branch, and say plainly that it
  precedes governed evidence.
- Ship the caller workflow as part of a documented ThreadLoop onboarding step rather than as part of the
  first feature branch.
- Consider whether a `repository_dispatch` or reusable-workflow invocation could avoid the default-branch
  requirement, and whether that weakens the signer identity guarantee. The current proof plan pins
  `certificate_identity` to `.github/workflows/threadloop.yml@refs/heads/<feature-branch>`, so any change
  here interacts with signer verification and must be designed, not improvised.

**Lifecycle state when recorded:** `verifying` v4, local proof `passed`, repair budget 3 of 3 remaining,
`pre_pr_review.status: not_started`, worktree clean at `6bed5d402d825c580d563518395281a8e6c85222`. No
override taken. No PR opened. No out-of-band commit.

## DX-2 (minor): `threadloop init` rejects `--json`

`threadloop init --json` fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT: unknown option '--json'`, while every other pilot
command accepts `--json`. An operator scripting setup has to special-case `init`.

## DX-3 (minor): the runner needs a CLI path that is not one of its four inputs

The runner contract takes exactly four inputs, none of which locates the `threadloop` binary. The pilot
installs the packaged CLI outside the consumer repository on purpose, so each wake invocation must be told
where it is. The fresh-context wake needed that path supplied alongside the four inputs. It is tooling
rather than lifecycle authority, but it is a real fifth thing an operator must convey.

## DX-4 (observation): review ordering is dictated by the projection, not by the plan

The refreshed execution plan sequenced local pre-PR reviews before signed CI. The live projection requires
`IMPORT_SIGNED_CI_PROOF` before `pre_pr_reviewing` becomes reachable. Running the local reviews first
anyway was still the right call, because it means signed CI is only ever spent on an already-reviewed HEAD,
but the plan's written order was wrong and the projection was right.

the provenance guarantee, so vendoring would trade away the property the signed receipt exists to provide.

  sharing with `access_level: user` is expected to work. That proves the mechanism but not the public-repo
  adoption path.

from __future__ import annotations

from copy import deepcopy
from typing import Annotated, Any

from fastapi import FastAPI, Header, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from signalpay_api.contracts import PaymentStatus, build_payment_event, verify_session


class Payment(BaseModel):
    payment_id: str = Field(alias="paymentId")
    customer_id: str = Field(alias="customerId")
    amount: int
    currency: str
    status: PaymentStatus

    model_config = {"populate_by_name": True}


# PAY-010: capture is authorized -> captured. Every other current status is a
# rejected transition, not a silent re-capture.
CAPTURABLE_STATUS = "authorized"

INITIAL_PAYMENTS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    "pay_1001": {
        "paymentId": "pay_1001",
        "customerId": "cus_9001",
        "amount": 12500,
        "currency": "USD",
        "status": "authorized",
    },
    "pay_1002": {
        "paymentId": "pay_1002",
        "customerId": "cus_9002",
        "amount": 4900,
        "currency": "USD",
        "status": "pending",
    },
}

payments: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = deepcopy(INITIAL_PAYMENTS)
payment_events: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
idempotency_results: dict[tuple[str, str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}

app = FastAPI(
    title="SignalPay Payments API",
    summary="Self-contained payments API for the Qodo quality-first workshop.",
    description=(
        "Use this API through `/docs` to practice planning, Qodo rules, "
        "local verification gates, PR review, and remediation."
    ),
)


def reset_state() -> None:
    """Reset in-memory state for tests and local workshop retries."""
    payments.clear()
    payments.update(deepcopy(INITIAL_PAYMENTS))
    payment_events.clear()
    idempotency_results.clear()


def require_principal(
    authorization: str | None,
    *,
    required_scope: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    if not authorization or not authorization.startswith("Bearer "):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Bearer session token is required")

    token = authorization.removeprefix("Bearer ").strip()
    try:
        principal = verify_session(token, "payments-api")
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail=str(exc)) from exc

    if required_scope and required_scope not in principal.scopes:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403,
            detail=f"{required_scope} scope is required",
        )


@app.get("/payments/{payment_id}", response_model=Payment, response_model_by_alias=True)
def get_payment(
    payment_id: str,
    authorization: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="Authorization")] = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require_principal(authorization)
    if payment_id not in payments:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="payment not found")
    return payments[payment_id]


@app.post("/payments/{payment_id}/capture", response_model=Payment, response_model_by_alias=True)
def capture_payment(
    payment_id: str,
    authorization: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="Authorization")] = None,
    idempotency_key: Annotated[
        str | None,
        Header(alias="Idempotency-Key"),
    ] = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require_principal(authorization, required_scope="payments:capture")
    if not idempotency_key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Idempotency-Key header is required")
    if payment_id not in payments:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="payment not found")

    result_key = ("capture", payment_id, idempotency_key)
    if result_key in idempotency_results:
        return idempotency_results[result_key]

    payment = payments[payment_id]
    # Runs after the exact-key replay above, so a retry still returns its original
    # response, and before any mutation, so a rejected transition emits no event
    # and stores no idempotency result.
    if payment["status"] != CAPTURABLE_STATUS:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409,
            detail=f"payment status {payment['status']} cannot begin a capture",
        )

    payment["status"] = "captured"

    event = build_payment_event(
        event_type="payment.captured",
        payment_id=payment["paymentId"],
        customer_id=payment["customerId"],
        amount=payment["amount"],
        currency=payment["currency"],
        status="captured",
    )
    payment_events.append(dict(event))
    idempotency_results[result_key] = deepcopy(payment)
    return payment

# SignalPay ThreadLoop Capture-State Pilot Report — Attempt 2

## Identity

- Pilot date: 2026-07-30
- SignalPay baseline: `a6e832cd8a5e031a3ea65729e04f1406ccf59b88`
- Pilot branch: `feat/threadloop-capture-state-pilot-2`
- Commits: `80d531c` enablement, `6bed5d4` feature, `9a487ca` pre-PR review fix
- ThreadLoop source: `6a59de94a354a4b0584e34cf98bfe5f4fc38a15f` (merged `main`)
- ThreadLoop package SHA-256: `8c0b61092ab8cd29fb79d901fb1e55e44970f934d651287c0fcfb686d55f8222`
- Runner skill SHA-256: `77d73d15555e9e2bf4df77f3275d5e7bb137103493d7fadb6469e6560d7de34b`
- Session: `session_81f8be12-1a3a-4d05-a806-f929933a7c45`
- Contracts: protocol 4, sessionNext 4, proofPlan 3, handoff 3, storage schema 7
- Proof plan digest: `08e7dda34dbf364391cbc69133dc4282d4fa2ea1ddde00dfb7a978501d2c7da2`

Attempt 1 (`session_535fdfc6-…`, branch `feat/threadloop-capture-state-pilot`) is untouched and remains at
`verifying` v4 on schema 6 as retained evidence.

## Headline result

**The lifecycle deadlock that ended Attempt 1 did not recur, and the capability that replaced it was
exercised end to end against a real consumer repository.**

Attempt 1 stopped because a confirmed pre-PR review finding had no authorized path back to local
repository work: `verifying` offered only `reviewing` (needs a PR) or `repairing` (consumes post-PR repair
budget and misclassifies the work). Attempt 2 performed exactly that previously impossible loop:

```text
verifying v4  --record pre_pr_review outcome (changes_required)-->  implementing v5
implementing v5  --COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION-->  commit 9a487ca
implementing v5  -->  verifying v6
verifying v6  --RERUN_STALE_GATES-->  proof passed at the new HEAD
```

Measured at every step: **repair budget stayed at 3 of 3 remaining with `attempts_used: 0`.** Pre-PR
iteration consumed none, which was the central requirement.

Three further properties the Attempt 1 observation document asked for were confirmed live:

- **HEAD-bound findings.** After commit `9a487ca`, `pre_pr_review.status` became `stale` and `proof.status`
  became `stale`, because both were bound to the superseded HEAD. ThreadLoop then required
  `RERUN_STALE_GATES` before anything else.
- **Multiple scoped commits before a PR.** Two feature commits landed pre-PR. Attempt 1's flow forced
  everything into one.
- **Fail-closed rejection with no side effects.** A probe transition attempted without review evidence was
  denied `PRE_PR_REVIEW_INPUT_REQUIRED` and reported
  `unchanged: [lifecycle, repair_budget, proof, review_evidence]`. Nothing moved.

## Measurements

- Total wakes: 9 records — 6 runner wakes, 3 operator/controller actions.
- Runner actions started: 6. Each performed exactly one action, then stopped.
- Operator actions: session start, proof-plan binding, pre-PR review outcome recording. All three carry
  non-empty input, so all three are operator authority by construction rather than by convention.
- Human interventions: 3 decisions (continuation strategy, unblocking DX-1, unblocking DX-5).
- Ambiguous or unknown stops: 0.
- Dirty-worktree or crash recovery: none. The worktree was clean at every preflight.
- Fresh-context continuation: **succeeded.** `pilot2-wake-005` ran in a separate cold process with only the
  repository, the skill, and the four inputs. It independently validated the full preflight, read
  `PROOF_GATES_MISSING -> RUN_MISSING_GATES` from the projection, ran only the `make-verify` gate, and
  stopped citing the non-idempotency rule. No transcript was supplied.
- Authority violations or duplicate effects: none observed. The runner never pushed, opened a PR, migrated
  schema, or ran a second action.
- Pre-PR review iterations: 1.
- Local gate runs: 2 (initial, then after the new HEAD staled the first).

## Review outcome

Four review results across two axes and two independent reviewers, all run before any push:

| Reviewer | Axis | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold process, tools disabled | Standards | CLEAN |
| Cold process, tools disabled | Spec | CLEAN, 7/7 requirements SATISFIED with cited lines |
| `code-review` skill in a cold process | Standards | CLEAN, one non-blocking nit |
| `code-review` skill in a cold process | Spec | CLEAN |

Attempt 1's confirmed P2 — capture auth rejections not proven side-effect free — was included in Attempt 2's
planned behavior from the start and confirmed satisfied by both reviewers. It did not recur.

The single nit (P3, untyped `CAPTURABLE_STATUS`) was resolved through the pre-PR iteration path rather than
an out-of-band commit. See `review-ledger.md`.

## Blocked: the arc did not reach `ready_for_human`

Two blockers stopped the signed-evidence half of the run. Both are recorded in `dx-findings.md`.

**DX-1**: `workflow_dispatch` resolves only from the default branch, so a consumer's first governed feature
branch cannot dispatch the sensor. Unblocked during the pilot by placing the caller workflow on SignalPay
`main` (commit `3000118`, pushed directly under explicit authorization, bypassing the PR convention the
rest of the repository follows — recorded here because that bypass is itself a deviation).

**DX-5, structural**: `nnennandukwe/threadloop` is private and SignalPay is public. Both sensor workflows
exist at the pinned SHA, but a public caller cannot consume a private repository's reusable workflow.
Granting owner-level Actions access (`access_level: user`) did not lift it; the setting was reverted to
`none`. Vendoring the sensor into the consumer would break the `build_signer_uri` provenance pinning the
signed receipt exists to provide, and would need a new session because the bound proof plan is immutable.

Consequence: `IMPORT_SIGNED_CI_PROOF` cannot be satisfied, so `pre_pr_reviewing`, `reviewing`, the feature
PR, signed review evidence, the post-PR repair path, `ready_for_human`, and the audit export were all not
reached.

## Final state

- Lifecycle: `verifying` v6, phase `pre_pr`
- Local proof: `passed` at `9a487ca2f4b97f9c2dc2112016c490c3c25e6530`, staleness `current`
- Gate receipts: `receipt_fc711340-…` (superseded), `receipt_c067431c-c559-4607-bc29-2a15acd4d312` (current)
- Repair budget: 3 of 3 remaining, 0 used
- `pre_pr_review`: `stale`, iteration_count 1
- Required work: `IMPORT_SIGNED_CI_PROOF` — blocked by DX-5
- Worktree: clean; branch pushed; **no PR opened**
- Audit status: `valid` throughout

## Assessment

On the question the pilot exists to answer, the lifecycle half is validated: a coding agent used the runner
skill across separate wakes, preserved lifecycle and proof state, iterated locally before a pull request
without consuming repair budget, and continued in a cold context. The fix for issue #69 works in a real
consumer repository, not only in ThreadLoop's own tests.

The signed-evidence half is unvalidated, and DX-5 is the reason. It is an adoption blocker rather than a
lifecycle defect: while ThreadLoop is private, it cannot govern a public consumer, because the provenance
guarantee depends on reusable workflows the consumer cannot reach.

The manual coordination cost was modest once running — the friction was concentrated in enablement, not in
the wake loop. Nothing observed here justifies building a controller or scheduler; the three operator
actions all exist because they carry evidence the runner is deliberately forbidden to synthesize, which is
a correct boundary rather than a missing feature.

- `pre_pr_review` going `stale` the instant HEAD moved is the load-bearing detail. Without it, a reviewer's "clean" verdict would silently outlive the code it examined — you'd carry approval across a commit that invalidated it. That's why binding findings to HEAD matters more than it sounds.
- GitHub validates *every* `uses:` reference at dispatch time, including jobs whose `if:` is false. Dispatching `evidence=gate` failed naming the **review** sensor. A workflow can't be partially reachable.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The loop Attempt 1 could not perform, executed live:

verifying v4  --record pre_pr_review (changes_required)-->  implementing v5
implementing v5  --COMMIT_IMPLEMENTATION-->  commit 9a487ca

**One correction to what I told you mid-run.** I said signed CI must land before the pre-PR review boundary. That's true for reaching `pre_pr_reviewing`, but wrong for pre-PR iteration — `verifying → implementing` needs only the review outcome. My first reading treated the single projected candidate as the only available path. The probe corrected it, and it's why the loop ran at all.

A=~/Code/threadloop-pilot-artifacts/signalpay-capture-state-attempt2; cat >> $A/dx-findings.md <<'EOF'

## DX-6 (blocking, root cause): the sensors clone ThreadLoop with no token, so they require a public ThreadLoop

**Observed at:** the first successful sensor dispatch, from a **private** throwaway consumer
(`nnennandukwe/threadloop-signed-chain-probe`) created specifically to test whether privacy symmetry would
lift DX-5.

**What changed and what did not:**

- With `access_level: user` on the private ThreadLoop and a *private* caller, `gh workflow run` **succeeded**.
  DX-5's diagnosis is therefore confirmed exactly: private-to-private reusable-workflow sharing works;
  public-to-private does not.
- The run then failed inside the sensor, repeatedly:

  ```text
  repository 'https://github.com/nnennandukwe/threadloop/' not found
  The process '/usr/bin/git' failed with exit code 128
  No files were found with the provided path: gate-observation/gate-report.json
  ```

**Root cause, in ThreadLoop's own workflow:** `.github/workflows/threadloop-gate-sensor.yml` checks out the
ThreadLoop repository to obtain the pinned CLI:

```yaml
- name: Check out pinned ThreadLoop sensor
  uses: actions/checkout@...
  with:
    repository: ${{ job.workflow_repository }}
    ref: ${{ job.workflow_sha }}
    path: threadloop-sensor
    persist-credentials: false
```

No `token:` is supplied, so the checkout authenticates with the **caller's** `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which is scoped
to the caller's repository. That token cannot read a private ThreadLoop, so the clone fails regardless of
the caller's own visibility. The review sensor has the identical step.

**Therefore:** making the consumer private does not rescue the signed-evidence chain. It moves the failure
from workflow *resolution* to workflow *runtime*. The sensors are built on the assumption that ThreadLoop is
publicly readable. No consumer configuration can satisfy them while it is private.

**Candidate remedies, none implemented:**

- Publish ThreadLoop, or publish the sensors plus the CLI they install. This is the assumption the sensors
  already encode.
- Add an optional token input to both sensors and pass it to that checkout, so a private-to-private
  deployment can supply a credential with read access to ThreadLoop. This is a small, contained change to
  two workflow files and is the only remedy that keeps ThreadLoop private.
- Install the CLI from a published package instead of checking out the repository, removing the clone
  entirely. Requires publishing the package.

**Probe state when recorded:** session `session_85d81bbd-92d5-4fda-b452-d244ffa75824` in
`nnennandukwe/threadloop-signed-chain-probe`, lifecycle `verifying` v4, local gate receipt
`receipt_ef96825d-da67-47cf-a605-a1516590fbab` passed at `79f98b4`, branch pushed, no PR opened. The local

The private consumer gave a cleaner answer than the public one, and it isn't the answer we wanted.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The private probe **narrowed** the problem rather than solving it. Dispatch succeeded, which proved DX-5's diagnosis exactly right (private→private sharing works, public→private doesn't). Then it failed one layer deeper. A negative result that relocates the failure is worth more than one that merely repeats it.
- The root cause is four lines of ThreadLoop's own workflow, not consumer misconfiguration. `repository: ${{ job.workflow_repository }}` with no `token:` authenticates using the **caller's** `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which is scoped to the caller's repo. `persist-credentials: false` is there for good hygiene, but nothing supplies a credential that can read a private ThreadLoop.
- So the sensors encode an unstated assumption: ThreadLoop is publicly readable. No consumer setting can satisfy them while it isn't — which is why "make the consumer private too" couldn't work, in hindsight.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## What the probe established

| Layer | Public consumer | Private consumer |
|---|---|---|
| Resolve reusable workflow | ✗ blocked (DX-5) | ✓ **works** with `access_level: user` |
| Clone ThreadLoop at runtime | not reached | ✗ **blocked** (DX-6) |
| Local gate + receipt | ✓ | ✓ `receipt_ef96825d…` at `79f98b4` |

The failing step, verbatim from the run: `repository 'https://github.com/nnennandukwe/threadloop/' not found` → `git failed with exit code 128` → `No files were found with the provided path: gate-observation/gate-report.json`.

Both sensors have the identical checkout, so signed review is blocked the same way.

## The narrow fix, if you want to keep ThreadLoop private

Add an optional token input to both sensor workflows and pass it to that one checkout. Two files, one `with:` line each, plus a documented secret in the consumer. That's the only remedy that preserves ThreadLoop's privacy — the other two (publish the repo, or install the CLI from a published package) both require publishing something.

Worth noting the sensors already work as designed *if* ThreadLoop is public. This isn't a bug so much as an undocumented deployment precondition.
